'''Subhash Chandra Lakhotia''' (born 4 October 1945) is an Indian [[cytogeneticist]], academic, Distinguished Professor<ref>{{cite web |title=Distinguished Professor |url=http://www.bhu.ac.in/science/zoology/faculty.php|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140122204320/http://www.bhu.ac.in/science/zoology/faculty.php|archive-date=22 January 2014}}</ref> of Zoology, and the [[Science & Engineering Research Board]] (SERB) Distinguished Fellow at the [[Banaras Hindu University]].<ref name="Faculty">{{cite web | url=http://www.bhu.ac.in/science/zoology/faculty.php | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140122204320/http://www.bhu.ac.in/science/zoology/faculty.php | archive-date=22 January 2014 | title=Faculty of Science | publisher=Banaras Hindu University | date=2016 | access-date=4 October 2016}}</ref> He is known for his pioneering research on [[Drosophila]] with regard to its chromosome organization and replication.<ref name="Brief">{{cite web | url=http://ssbprize.gov.in/Content/Detail.aspx?AID=169 | title=Brief Profile of the Awardee | publisher=Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize | date=2016 | access-date=28 September 2016}}</ref> A [[Raja Ramanna]] fellow of the [[Department of Science and Technology (India)|Department of Science and Technology]] and the [[Department of Atomic Energy]], he is an elected fellow of all three major Indian science academies: [[Indian National Science Academy]], [[Indian Academy of Sciences]] and [[National Academy of Sciences, India]].<ref name="Fellow">{{cite web | url=http://insaindia.res.in/detail.php?id=N93-1123 | title=Indian Fellow - Lakhotia | publisher=Indian National Science Academy | date=2016 | access-date=30 September 2016}}</ref> He is a Senior Fellow of the Cell Stress Society International (USA). The [[Council of Scientific and Industrial Research]], the apex agency of the Government of India for scientific research, awarded him the [[Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize for Science and Technology]], one of the highest Indian science awards, in 1989, for his contributions to biological sciences.<ref name="View">{{cite web | url=http://ssbprize.gov.in/Content/AwardeeList.aspx | title=View Bhatnagar Awardees | publisher=Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize | date=2016 | access-date=19 September 2016}}</ref>

== Biography ==
[[File:BHU Main Gate, Banaras Hindu University.jpg|thumb|235px|[[Banaras Hindu University]]]]
Subhash Chandra Lakhotia was born on 4 October 1945 in [[Churu, Rajasthan|Churu]], a city near [[Thar Desert]] in the Indian state of [[Rajasthan]], to Dwarka Prasad-Suryakala couple.<ref name="Chandra Lakhotia">{{cite web | url=https://www.myheritage.com/names/chandra_lakhotia?lang=AR | title=Chandra Lakhotia | publisher=My Heritage | date=2016 | access-date=4 October 2016}}</ref> He did his early schooling in Churu and then in Kolkata.

He graduated from [[Vidyasagar College]] of the [[University of Calcutta|Calcutta University]] in Zoology Honours in 1964 before obtaining his master's degree in Zoology and [[Comparative anatomy|Comparative Anatomy]] in 1966, both from the Calcutta University.<ref name="Fellow"/> Continuing his doctoral studies at the same university at the Zoology Department, he secured his PhD in 1970. He did his post-doctoral studies at [[Delhi University]] during 1970–71 and started his career as a lecturer at [[Burdwan University]] in 1971. Moving to [[Gujarat University]] in June 1972, he stayed there until September 1976 before joining the [[Banaras Hindu University]] as a reader. He became a full professor in 1984 and continued there until superannuation in 2010. In between, he carried out some advanced studies at the Institute of Animal Genetics of the [[University of Edinburgh]] during 1972-73, at the [[University of California, Irvine]] during 1984-85 and at [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]], Cambridge in 1985. After his formal superannuation, he continued his academic activities at the Banaras Hindu University as Emeritus Professor, INSA senior scientist from January 2017 to January 2019 <ref name="Fellow"/> and is now working as the life-long Distinguished Professor and SERB Distinguished Fellow.

== Legacy ==
[[File:Drosophila melanogaster - side (aka).jpg|thumb|170px|left|[[Drosophila melanogaster]]]]
Lakhotia's research is focused on cytogenetics, [[gene expression]], cell and developmental biology.<ref name="Handbook">{{cite web | url=http://www.csirhrdg.res.in/ssb.pdf | title=Handbook of Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize Winners | publisher=Council of Scientific and Industrial Research | date=1999 | access-date=28 September 2016 | page=29}}</ref> He carried out pioneering research on [[Drosophila]] (fruit flies) with regards to its chromosome organization and replication, tissue-specific differences in expression of [[heat shock protein]]s, and discovery of [[Hsp90|Hsp60]] in [[Drosophila]]. He has carried out life-time studies on the organization and functions of the 93D or the [[Hsromega|hsromega gene]] long-non-coding RNA locus of [[Drosophila melanogaster]].<ref name="ias jbsc">{{Cite web| title=Forty years of the 93D puff of Drosophila melanogaster | url=https://www.ias.ac.in/article/fulltext/jbsc/036/03/0399-0423 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180722155618/https://www.ias.ac.in/article/fulltext/jbsc/036/03/0399-0423 | archive-date=2018-07-22}}</ref> During his doctoral studies on [[dosage compensation]] in Drosophila he further confirmed the hyperactive male-X model and elucidated its cellular autonomy.<ref>{{cite book|title=Advances in Genetics|url=https://archive.org/details/advancesingeneti0041unse|url-access=registration|date=4 May 1999|publisher=Academic Press|isbn=978-0-08-056826-3|pages=[https://archive.org/details/advancesingeneti0041unse/page/81 81]–}}</ref> His discovery of active transcription in [[heterochromatin]] in Drosophila in early 1970s was one of the first documentations of transcriptional activity of heterochromatin. His later studies revealed the existence of two distinct [[Replicon (genetics)|replicon]] types in different cell types of Drosophila.

He has been a pioneer researcher studying the long [[non-coding RNA]]s since 1980s and has contributed significantly to a wider appreciation of their function through sustained studies on the [[Hsromega|hsromega gene]].<ref name="ias jbsc"/> His laboratory discovered the omega speckles<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Prasanth |first1=K.V. |last2=Rajendra |first2=T.K. |last3=Lal |first3=A.K. |last4=Lakhotia |first4=S.C. |year=2000 |title=Omega speckles - a novel class of nuclear speckles containing HNRNPS associated with noncoding HSR-omega RNA in Drosophila |url=http://jcs.biologists.org/content/113/19/3485 |journal=[[Journal of Cell Science]] |volume=113 |issue=19 |pages=3485–3497 |doi=10.1242/jcs.113.19.3485 |pmid=10984439|url-access=subscription }}</ref> in Drosophila nuclei and established essential functions of the lncRNAs produced by the [[Hsromega|hsromega gene]] in organization of the intra-nuclear omega speckles. His studies also helped identify how this lncRNA gene modulates [[apoptosis]] and [[neurodegeneration]] in Drosophila models of human diseases.
 
Since 2008, he established Drosophila as a good model to understand the mechanisms of actions of some of the [[ayurvedic]] formulations.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Dwivedi |first1=Vibha |last2=Anandan |first2=E. M. |last3=Mony |first3=Rajesh S. |last4=Muraleedharan |first4=T. S. |last5=Valiathan |first5=M. S. |last6=Mutsuddi |first6=Mousumi |last7=Lakhotia |first7=Subhash C. |year=2012 |title=In Vivo Effects of Traditional Ayurvedic Formulations in Drosophila melanogaster Model Relate with Therapeutic Applications |journal=[[PLOS ONE]] |volume=7 |issue=5 |article-number=e37113 |bibcode=2012PLoSO...737113D |doi=10.1371/journal.pone.0037113 |pmc=3351451 |pmid=22606337 |doi-access=free}}</ref> His studies indicate that the Ayurvedic Amalaki Rasayana and Rasa-Sindoor can substantially suppress neurodegeneration associated with [[Trinucleotide repeat disorder|polyQ]] and Alzheimer's disorders.

He has published more than 200 original research papers, review articles, and chapters in books, available at [[PubMed]], an online repository of medical articles,<ref name="PubMed">{{cite web | url=https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/?term=Lakhotia%20SC%5BAuthor%5D&cauthor=true&cauthor_uid=2517262 | title=Lakhotia on PubMed | publisher=PubMed | work=Author profile | date=2016 | access-date=4 October 2016}}</ref> and at [[ResearchGate]].<ref name="ResearchGate">{{cite web | url=https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Subhash_Lakhotia | title=Subhash Chandra Lakhotia on ResearchGate | date=2016 | access-date=4 October 2016}}</ref> He has also written more than 100 articles relating to policies on higher education, research publications, their assessment and ethics.

He has mentored more than 35 scholars in their doctoral studies.<ref name="Fellow"/>

Lakhotia contributed to the establishment of the Department of Molecular and Human Genetics at the Banaras Hindu University and to the installation of the [[Confocal microscopy|Confocal microscope]] facility at his department.<ref name="Fellow"/>

Besides his research contributions, Lakhotia is also well known for his many writings on education.<ref name="ResearchGate"/> He served as a member of one of the sub-committees of the [[National Knowledge Commission]], participated in the Committee on Science Education of the [[International Council for Science]] (ICSU) in 2010 and was a member of its review panel.<ref name="Review">{{cite web | url=http://www.icsu.org/what-we-do/committees/science-education-review/?icsudocid=panel-members | title=Review Panel members | publisher=International Council for Science | date=2016 | access-date=4 October 2016}}</ref> He was associated with the [[International Union of Biological Sciences]], as a member of its executive committee from 2000 to 2003 and later as its vice president from 2003 to 2006.<ref name="IUBS boards">{{cite web | url=https://www.iubs.org/iubs/pastboards.html | title=IUBS boards | publisher=International Union of Biological Sciences | date=2016 | access-date=4 October 2016}}</ref> He is a former member of the INSA council, a former vice president,<ref name="VP">{{cite web | url=http://insaindia.res.in/recent_past_office_bearers.php | title=Recent Past Vice-presidents | publisher=INSA | date=2016 | access-date=4 October 2016 | archive-date=1 May 2021 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210501055419/https://www.insaindia.res.in/recent_past_office_bearers.php }}</ref> and vice president of its Inter-Academy Exchange Committee.<ref name="IA">{{cite web | url=http://insaindia.res.in/advisory.php | title=Inter-Academy Exchange Committee | publisher=INSA | date=2016 | access-date=4 October 2016}}</ref> He was the editor-in-chief of its journal (''Proceedings of the Indian National Science Academy'') from January 2014 to December 2018. He has been associated with the [[Council of Scientific and Industrial Research]], [[University Grants Commission of India]], [[Department of Atomic Energy]], [[Department of Science and Technology (India)|Department of Science and Technology]] and [[Department of Biotechnology]] as a member of their various committees,<ref name="Fellow"/> and has served or is continuing as a member of the editorial boards of journals such as ''[[Current Science]]'', ''[[Journal of Biosciences]]'', ''[[RNA Biology]]'', ''Cell Stress and Chaperones'' and ''Annals of Neurosciences''. He is a life member of the Indian Society of Cell Biology, Indian Society of Developmental Biology, Cell Stress Society International, [[Genetics Society of America]] and [[RNA Society]].<ref name="experience">{{cite web | url=https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Subhash_Lakhotia/info | title=Subhash Chandra Lakhotia - Research experience | date=2016 | access-date=4 October 2016}}</ref>

== Awards and honors ==
Lakhotia received the Young Scientists Medal of the [[Indian National Science Academy]] in 1975<ref name="Young Scientists Medal">{{cite web | url=http://insaindia.res.in/youngmedal.php | title=Young Scientists Medal | publisher=Indian National Science Academy | date=2016 | access-date=4 October 2016 | archive-date=11 May 2021 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210511084357/https://www.insaindia.res.in/youngmedal.php }}</ref> and the Career Award in Sciences of the [[University Grants Commission of India]] (UGC) in 1979. The [[Council of Scientific and Industrial Research]] awarded him the [[Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize]], one of the highest Indian science awards, in 1989,<ref name="View" /> the same year that he was selected as the National Lecturer by the UGC. The Commission honored him again in 1998 with the [[Jagadish Chandra Bose|J.C. Bose]] Award, and he received INSA [[Sunder Lal Hora]] Medal in 2002.<ref name="Medal">{{cite web | url=http://insaindia.res.in/recipients.php#56 | title=The Sunder Lal Hora Medal | publisher=INSA | date=2016 | access-date=4 October 2016 | archive-date=16 September 2016 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160916233840/http://insaindia.res.in/recipients.php#56 }}</ref> The Banaras Hindu University gave him the 2007 Professor [[C. N. R. Rao|CNR Rao]] Education Foundation Award.<ref name="experience" />

Lakhotia has held the Ramanna fellowship of the [[Department of Science and Technology (India)|Department of Science and Technology]] from 2009 and the Raja Ramanna Fellowship of the [[Department of Atomic Energy]] from 2011. He held the Jawaharlal Nehru Birth Centenary Fellowship and the Senior Scientist position of the Indian National Science Academy in 2009. He was elected as a fellow by the Indian National Science Academy in 1993, by the [[Indian Academy of Sciences]] in 1994<ref name="FP">{{cite web | url=http://www.ias.ac.in/describe/fellow/Lakhotia,_Prof._Subhash_Chandra | title=Fellow profile - Indian Academy of Sciences | publisher=Indian Academy of Sciences | date=2016 | access-date=30 September 2016}}</ref> and by the [[National Academy of Sciences, India]] in 2002.<ref name="NASI fellows">{{cite web | url=http://www.nasi.org.in/fellows.asp?RsFilter=L | title=NASI fellows | publisher=National Academy of Sciences, India | date=2016 | access-date=3 October 2016 | archive-date=12 October 2020 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201012031249/http://www.nasi.org.in/fellows.asp?RsFilter=L }}</ref> He was awarded the Joy Gobind Law Memorial Medal ij 2022 by the [[The Asiatic Society|Asiatic Society, Kolkata]].

He has delivered several award lectures, including the 18th G.J.S. Rao Memorial Award Lecture of the [[Indian Institute of Science]] in 2011, the [[Aryabhata|Arya Bhatta]] Medal lecture of the Indian National Science Academy (2018)<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://insaindia.res.in/detail/N93-1123 |title=INSA :: Indian Fellow Detail |access-date=14 April 2019 |archive-date=14 April 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190414014559/http://insaindia.res.in/detail/N93-1123 }}</ref> and the IASTAM Zandu International (Indian Citizen) Award for Excellence in Field of Ayurveda and/or Natural Products Award 2019.<ref>{{Cite web| title=10 th series of IASTAM Oration and Awards and Conclave on AYUSH & Cancer | url=http://www.iastamindia.org/wp-content/uploads/2019/03/28-III4IASTAMNewsletterMar-2019.pdf | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190414014600/http://www.iastamindia.org/wp-content/uploads/2019/03/28-III4IASTAMNewsletterMar-2019.pdf | archive-date=2019-04-14}}</ref> In 2019, he was awarded the SERB Distinguished Fellowship (2019).<ref>{{Cite web| title=Recommendations of the High-Level Selection Committee on the nominations received for SERB Distinguished Fellowship | url=http://serb.gov.in/pdfs/Results/results%20DF.pdf | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190214163510/http://serb.gov.in:80/pdfs/Results/results%20DF.pdf | archive-date=2019-02-14}}</ref>
